_provenance_tier3.producer: RFC 7748 §5.2 (Elliptic Curves for Security), iteration-1 Diffie-Hellman test vectors
_provenance_tier3.note: WS-5.3 (2026-08-30): this repo has no local RFC 7748 text (checked docs/refs/ — absent) and per this project's standing policy specs are read from vendored local copies, never freshly web-fetched. These two constants (k0=u0=9 for X25519, k0=u0=5 for X448, both first-byte-only with the rest zero, per RFC 7748's own iterative test construction where iteration 1 is exactly X(k0, u0)) are copied byte-for-byte from rust/src/native/encrypt.rs's own x25519_rfc7748_iterative_1 / x448_rfc7748_iterative_1 unit tests (lines ~1961, ~1997), which are already vendored, CI-verified, and independently cite the same RFC section. Not re-derived from memory. Verified independently against this C++ engine via both the spec-correct CKM_ECDH1_DERIVE mechanism (PKCS#11 v3.2 §6.3.11 — the only derive mechanism the ratified spec actually defines for Montgomery curves; confirmed by reading docs/refs/pkcs11-spec-v3.2-os.pdf directly, not assumed) and this engine's additional vendor-range CKM_X25519/CKM_X448 mechanisms (SoftHSM_keygen.cpp dispatches both to the identical code path).
